title: US vs. UK Safety Institute: Divergent Evaluation Methodologies

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: divergent evaluation methodologies from the two most prominent safety institutes would directly undermine international evaluation consensus. Finding is immediately policy-relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: comparing evaluation methodologies in depth requires understanding of model evaluation techniques and the ability to analyze technical reports critically. Beginners would need guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: collecting evaluation reports from both institutes, systematically comparing metrics/categories/conclusions for each co-evaluated model. Feasible but requires careful work.

novelty.reasoning: The divergence between US and UK AI safety institutes is well-documented. The two institutes conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of OpenAI's o1 model (December 2024) running 'separate but complementary tests.' The UK renamed to AI Security Institute (Feb 2025), the US renamed to Center for AI Standards and Innovation (June 2025). All Tech Is Human published 'The Global Landscape of AI Safety Institutes' and CSIS published recommendations for the AISI International Network. The UK published its Frontier AI Trends Report (2025) and Autonomous Systems Evaluation Standard. However, a systematic side-by-side comparison of their evaluation methodologies for co-evaluated models has not been published. The institutional divergence is described but the technical evaluation methodology comparison gap remains partially open.
